chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
"The fingers of the hands and feet are equal in compensation (diyyah)."

And he said: "Regarding a tooth, when it is struck, one should wait with it for a year. If it falls out, the striker must pay five hundred dirhams. If it does not fall out but turns black, he must pay two-thirds of its compensation."

key_terms.أَصَابِعُ ٱلْيَدَيْنِ وَ ٱلرِّجْلَيْنِ: the fingers of the hands and feet as a legal category of injury
key_terms.خَمْسَمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: five hundred dirhams as the specified compensation
key_terms.ٱسْوَدَّتْ: it turned black, indicating lasting injury short of falling out
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.ٱلسِّنِّ: a tooth, in the context of injury compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for injured fingers and a struck tooth in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning diyyah for bodily injury. It establishes that the fingers of the hands and feet carry equal compensation, and it details the compensation for a struck tooth based on whether it falls out after observation for a year or remains but turns black.
